questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Limited places that offer english speaking courses, so I chose within nordic countries because of danish/norwegian capabilities gave wider course options. NMBU had some interesting sounding courses. I also wanted a break from climate activism, so Trondheim where the oil/gas sector has mayor opreations were not an option. And so NMBU it was.

Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the staff at NMBU is very helpful!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Intro meeting and help from other erasmus students abroad.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing and private housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Kitchens in all appartments

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Its great to be so close to other exchange students. Worth to rent kitchenware.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite similar to danish system.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Sign up through online portal

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The staff at NMBU very helpful and sent out good information.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up to more courses than you plan to take, the deadline for dropping out of an exam is quite late, so you can attend courses that sound interesting and find out if they are actually good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a bit disappointed with quite low expectations to the students in some courses, and others quite disorganized.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses were mixed bachelor/master courses. Level between courses varied, especially the expectations to the students. Some were quite easy, some fitting. I did 30 points but I had more than enough time, I think I could have done another course. There was very little reading in courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, mixture of lectures, exercises and hand-ins.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. NMBU is a very easy place to be an exchange student.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything basically!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Climbing, frluftsliv. 
Lot of fun and a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Oslomarken

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, not a big difference between norway and denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the whatsapp groups, join the parties, just say yes to a lot of things in the beginning to find some people to hang out with. Join a club or begin climbing/bouldering.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
the attitude towards outdoor life. 
+ Students at NMBU very open and welcoming to exchange students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you are there for acedemia - then sign up for more courses than you plan to take, you can always dump some of them after. 
Plan a trip with some new exchange friends to see some more of Norway, Ås is not too exotic.
Join the Foodsharing group, super nice ppl.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go see Norway! Prioritize spending some money to travel. You can borrow outdoor equipment from Friluftsliv.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Taking a break from my life back home, made me very happy yo come back.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing people dear to me. Being frustrated about not being challenge as much as I hoped acedemically.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
